global_lexicon.core_thesis: An interpretable machine-learning framework combining Extra Trees benchmarking, multi-model SHAP interpretability, and manifold-constrained feasibility sampling establishes an actionable, multi-objective operational basin for a full-scale semiconductor wastewater membrane bioreactor, identifying sludge retention time (SRT) as the dominant fouling driver and raising simultaneous target attainment from 37% to over 61–82%.

key_terms.definition: Membrane bioreactor, an integrated biological treatment and membrane filtration (submerged PVDF hollow-fibre) process for wastewater purification.
Transmembrane pressure, the pressure gradient driving water permeation across the membrane and principal indicator of membrane fouling.
Treated effluent flow rate drawn through the membrane module by suction pump, with target >= 1.5 m3/min.
Liquid level in the membrane tank serving as an integrative hydraulic state variable reflecting hydraulic balance and solids accumulation.
Sludge retention time (mean solids residence time in the bioreactor), identified as the dominant driver of TMP and fouling across the 43.3–108.3 day extended-aeration regime.
Hydraulic retention time (liquid residence time in the biological reactor), acting as a sharp hydraulic lever controlling throughput and membrane loading.
Mixed liquor suspended solids concentration in the bioreactor, exhibiting non-monotonic scaling with cake resistance.
Food-to-microorganism ratio, representing organic substrate loading rate per unit of active microbial biomass.
SHapley Additive exPlanations, a cooperative game-theoretic framework evaluating feature importance and non-linear interactions across models.
Extremely Randomized Trees ensemble regressor, achieving highest accuracy and robustness across random, blocked, chronological, and parallel-train validations.
Feasibility sampling method perturbing states along local covariance within the plant's reachable space (500,000 samples) rather than independent marginal ranges.
Proportion of operating hours simultaneously satisfying TMP <= 0.15 bar, permeate flow >= 1.5 m3/min, and membrane tank level 58–60%.

key_entities: Asan City semiconductor wastewater treatment plant

global_context_pack:
Core Thesis:
An interpretable machine-learning framework combining Extra Trees benchmarking, multi-model SHAP interpretability, and manifold-constrained feasibility sampling establishes an actionable, multi-objective operational basin for a full-scale semiconductor wastewater membrane bioreactor, identifying sludge retention time (SRT) as the dominant fouling driver and raising simultaneous target attainment from 37% to over 61–82%.

Glossary of Terms & Acronyms:
- MBR: Membrane Bioreactor (submerged PVDF hollow-fibre ultrafiltration with biological degradation)
- TMP: Transmembrane Pressure (fouling indicator; target <= 0.15 bar)
- Flow: Permeate Flow rate (production target >= 1.5 m3/min)
- Level: Membrane Tank Water Level (hydraulic balance target 58–60%)
- SRT: Sludge Retention Time (operational range 43.3–108.3 days)
- HRT: Hydraulic Retention Time (operational range 5.0–12.0 hours)
- MLSS: Mixed Liquor Suspended Solids (operational range 1919–7629 mg/L)
- F/M: Food-to-Microorganism ratio (operational range 0.012–0.066 day^-1)
- Glu: Glucose dosing rate (supplemental carbon source, 0.40–1.35 L/min)
- Air: Membrane aeration scouring rate (operational range 4469–7268 m3/h)
- C/N: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio (operational range 4.80–17.50)
- SHAP: SHapley Additive exPlanations (TreeSHAP and KernelSHAP)
- SCADA: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (4593 continuous hourly records)
- KDE: Kernel Density Estimation (Gaussian kernel, Scott's rule)

Document Structure Overview:
- 1. Introduction: Full-scale semiconductor wastewater challenges, complex organic/chemical loading, and multi-objective optimization objectives.
- 2. Models and methods: Full-scale system (1,125 m3/h in Asan City), data standardisation, four rigorous validation designs (random 70/30, 20-split, blocked 1–720 h, chronological out-of-time, and independent parallel train B), benchmarking of 16 algorithms across 6 families, multi-model SHAP interpretability, and manifold-constrained feasibility sampling.
- 3. Results and discussion:
  - 3.1. Predictive performance: Extra Trees superiority (R2 = 0.988 for TMP, 0.933 for Flow, 0.908 for Level) and stability across all temporal and external validation schemes.
  - 3.2. Process interpretability: 16-model SHAP consensus proving SRT as the dominant fouling driver across extended aeration; non-monotonic HRT, aeration, and MLSS dynamics.
  - 3.3. Operational basin: Derivation of the evidence-graded operating window (SRT 43.2–72.2 d, HRT 5.9–6.4 h, MLSS 5580–6138 mg/L, F/M 0.023–0.025 d^-1, aeration 4868–5892 m3/h), achieving 61–82% target attainment, validated on out-of-time data (OR = 3.89).
  - 3.4. Comparative perspectives: Comparison against single-target and black-box pilot studies, highlighting the value of dual-context interpretability and joint-manifold exploration.
- 4. Conclusion & Appendix: Methodological transferability to other industrial MBRs and open-source data availability.
